description: Study of triangle relationships and periodic functions. Covers right-triangle trigonometry, the unit circle, trigonometric functions and their graphs, identities, equations, and the laws of sines and cosines.

concepts.title: Angle Measurement in Degrees
learning_objectives: Measure and classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, or straight
Identify complementary and supplementary angle pairs
Convert between degrees, minutes, and seconds (DMS) and decimal degrees

concepts.title: Radian Measure
learning_objectives: Define a radian as the ratio of arc length to radius
Convert between degree and radian measure
Calculate arc length and sector area using radians

concepts.title: Angles in Standard Position
learning_objectives: Sketch angles in standard position on the coordinate plane
Identify coterminal angles and find them by adding or subtracting full rotations
Determine the reference angle for any angle in standard position

concepts.title: Angular and Linear Speed
learning_objectives: Calculate angular speed in radians per unit time
Relate angular speed to linear speed via v = rω
Solve applied problems involving rotating objects

concepts.title: Trigonometric Ratios
learning_objectives: Define sine, cosine, and tangent as ratios of sides of a right triangle
Define cosecant, secant, and cotangent as reciprocals of the primary ratios
Evaluate trigonometric ratios for given right triangles

concepts.title: Solving Right Triangles
learning_objectives: Find unknown sides and angles of a right triangle using trigonometric ratios
Apply the Pythagorean theorem in conjunction with trigonometric ratios
Solve applied problems involving angles of elevation and depression

concepts.title: Trigonometric Functions of Special Angles
learning_objectives: Evaluate exact trigonometric values for 30°, 45°, and 60° angles
Derive these values from the 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 reference triangles
Apply special angle values to simplify expressions

concepts.title: Applications of Right Triangle Trigonometry
learning_objectives: Solve navigation and bearing problems using right triangle trigonometry
Calculate heights and distances using indirect measurement
Model and solve real-world problems involving right triangles

concepts.title: Unit Circle Definition of Trigonometric Functions
learning_objectives: Define sin θ and cos θ as coordinates of the point on the unit circle corresponding to angle θ
Evaluate trigonometric functions for quadrantal angles (0, π/2, π, 3π/2)
Determine the sign of each trigonometric function in each quadrant

concepts.title: Reference Angles and the Unit Circle
learning_objectives: Use reference angles to evaluate trigonometric functions for any angle
Reproduce exact values for all multiples of π/6 and π/4 on the unit circle
Evaluate trigonometric functions for negative angles and angles beyond 2π

concepts.title: Properties of the Trigonometric Functions
learning_objectives: Identify the domain and range of each of the six trigonometric functions
Classify each trigonometric function as even or odd
State the period of each trigonometric function

concepts.title: Graphs of Sine and Cosine
learning_objectives: Graph y = sin x and y = cos x over multiple periods
Identify the amplitude, period, and midline of a sinusoidal function
Graph y = A sin(Bx − C) + D and y = A cos(Bx − C) + D with transformations

concepts.title: Graphs of Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and Cosecant
learning_objectives: Graph y = tan x and y = cot x, identifying period and vertical asymptotes
Graph y = sec x and y = csc x, identifying period and vertical asymptotes
Apply transformations to the graphs of all six trigonometric functions

concepts.title: Sinusoidal Modeling
learning_objectives: Determine amplitude, period, phase shift, and vertical shift from real-world data
Write a sinusoidal function to model periodic phenomena (tides, temperature, sound)
Use a sinusoidal model to make predictions

concepts.title: Fundamental Identities
learning_objectives: State and apply the Pythagorean identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and its variants
Apply reciprocal and quotient identities to simplify expressions
Simplify trigonometric expressions using fundamental identities

concepts.title: Proving Trigonometric Identities
learning_objectives: Verify a trigonometric identity by transforming one side to match the other
Select appropriate strategies: work from the more complex side, convert to sines and cosines, factor
Distinguish between conditional equations and identities

concepts.title: Sum and Difference Formulas
learning_objectives: Apply the sum and difference formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent
Evaluate exact trigonometric values for non-standard angles like 15° and 75°
Use sum and difference formulas to prove or derive other identities

concepts.title: Double-Angle and Half-Angle Formulas
learning_objectives: Derive and apply double-angle formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent
Derive and apply half-angle formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent
Use these formulas to simplify expressions and solve equations

concepts.title: Inverse Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
learning_objectives: Define arcsin, arccos, and arctan with their restricted domains and ranges
Evaluate inverse trigonometric functions for exact and approximate values
Compose trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions

concepts.title: Solving Trigonometric Equations
learning_objectives: Solve basic trigonometric equations on a given interval
Solve trigonometric equations requiring factoring or the quadratic formula
Find all solutions of a trigonometric equation using periodicity

concepts.title: Solving Advanced Trigonometric Equations
learning_objectives: Solve equations involving multiple angles using double-angle or half-angle formulas
Solve equations requiring sum-to-product or product-to-sum transformations
Solve applied trigonometric equations in context

concepts.title: Law of Sines
learning_objectives: State and apply the law of sines to solve ASA and AAS triangles
Identify and resolve the ambiguous case (SSA) using the law of sines
Determine when a triangle has zero, one, or two solutions

concepts.title: Law of Cosines
learning_objectives: State and apply the law of cosines to solve SAS and SSS triangles
Recognize when to use the law of cosines versus the law of sines
Derive the law of cosines from the distance formula

concepts.title: Area of Triangles
learning_objectives: Calculate the area of a triangle using A = ½ ab sin C
Apply Heron's formula when three sides are known
Solve applied problems involving area of non-right triangles

concepts.title: Polar Coordinates
learning_objectives: Plot points in the polar coordinate system
Convert between polar and rectangular coordinates
Graph basic polar equations (circles, cardioids, roses)

concepts.title: Vectors in Two Dimensions
learning_objectives: Represent vectors graphically and in component form
Compute vector addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication
Calculate the magnitude and direction angle of a vector

concepts.title: The Dot Product
learning_objectives: Compute the dot product of two vectors
Use the dot product to find the angle between two vectors
Determine whether two vectors are orthogonal using the dot product

concepts.title: Applications of Vectors
learning_objectives: Decompose a force vector into horizontal and vertical components
Solve equilibrium and resultant force problems
Compute work as a dot product of force and displacement vectors

projects.title: Mapping a Terrain with Triangulation
projects.description: Use the law of sines and cosines to determine distances and positions of landmarks from two observation points. Create a scaled map from angle and distance measurements.
learning_objectives: Apply oblique triangle solving techniques to a surveying scenario
Select the appropriate law (sines vs. cosines) based on known information
Calculate areas and distances from indirect measurements

projects.title: Modeling Daylight Hours with Sinusoidal Functions
projects.description: Using real daylight-hour data for a chosen latitude, fit a sinusoidal model, predict sunrise and sunset times, and compare the model to the equinox and solstice data.
learning_objectives: Extract amplitude, period, and phase shift from real-world data
Write and validate a sinusoidal model
Interpret model parameters in a physical context

projects.title: Prove the Angle Addition Formulas Geometrically
projects.description: Construct a geometric proof of the cosine sum formula using the unit circle and the distance formula, then derive the sine sum formula as a corollary.
learning_objectives: Construct a rigorous geometric argument from unit circle definitions
Apply the distance formula to derive an algebraic identity
Extend a result to derive related identities
